title: SAP BTP: qué es y componentes principales
tags: btp, business technology platform, cloud, paas
excerpt: Introducción a SAP BTP y sus servicios core.
body:
## SAP BTP
SAP Business Technology Platform — PaaS de SAP para:
- Extend SAP apps (ECC, S/4HANA, SuccessFactors, etc.)
- Build custom apps
- Data + analytics
- Integration
- AI / ML services

## Layers

### Application Development
- **Cloud Foundry (CF)** — main runtime
- **Kyma** — Kubernetes-based runtime
- **ABAP environment** — steampunk (ABAP en cloud)
- **HTML5 apps** — Fiori launchpad hosting

### Integration
- **Integration Suite** — ESB en cloud
- **API Management**
- **Event Mesh** — event-driven
- **Cloud Connector** — hybrid connectivity (on-prem)

### Data & Analytics
- **HANA Cloud** — DB managed
- **Datasphere** — data warehouse
- **Analytics Cloud (SAC)** — BI + planning
- **Data Intelligence** — ETL / MLOps

### Extension
- **Extension Suite** — dev tools
- **Build Apps** — low-code
- **Business Application Studio** — IDE cloud

### AI
- **AI Core** — model deployment
- **AI Launchpad** — model management
- **Joule** — generative AI copilot

## Regions
BTP available en múltiples regions (each = data center):
- AWS Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland)
- AWS US (Ashburn, San Jose)
- AWS Asia (Tokyo, Sydney, Singapore)
- Azure Europe (Netherlands, France)
- GCP US (Iowa)
- Alibaba China

Choose based on:
- Data residency
- Latency to users
- Compliance

## Structure
### Global Account
Top-level container per SAP customer.

### Directories
Optional grouping (departments, projects).

### Subaccounts
Actual workspaces:
- Region-specific
- Entitled services
- Users + roles
- Environments (CF, Kyma, ABAP)

## Cost model
- **CPEA** (Consumption Pattern for Enterprise Agreements) — pay-as-you-go from cloud credits
- **Subscription** — fixed price per service

## Login
User: BTP cockpit https://account.hana.ondemand.com o https://<region>.hana.ondemand.com

Auth via corporate IdP (SAML SSO) o SAP Universal ID.

## Free tier
**BTP Free Tier**: services with reduced quota gratis. Perfect for learning.

Sign up: https://www.sap.com/products/technology-platform/trial.html

## Cockpit walkthrough
- **Global Account** overview
- **Subaccounts** list
- **Users** management
- **Entitlements** (services enabled)
- **Subscriptions**
- **Cost** monitoring
- **Downloads** (tools like SCC, SAPUI5)

## Common terms
- **Space** — CF namespace within subaccount
- **App** — deployed application instance
- **Service instance** — managed service (DB, Redis, etc.)
- **Binding** — link app ↔ service instance
- **Route** — URL mapping to app

## First steps
1. Access cockpit
2. Explore subaccount
3. Enable CF environment
4. Create space
5. Deploy sample app
6. Explore services

## Resources
- SAP Learning Hub
- SAP Help portal https://help.sap.com/btp
- SAP Community (community.sap.com)
- OpenSAP courses (free)

## Roadmap awareness
- SAP focus: S/4HANA + BTP is core cloud strategy
- Integration Suite y HANA Cloud siendo development activo
- Legacy: Neo environment being deprecated (2028), migrate to CF/Kyma

title: SAP BTP: Global Account, Directory, Subaccount hierarchy
tags: btp, global account, directory, subaccount, organization
excerpt: Estructura organizativa de BTP: cómo dividir workloads.
body:
## Global Account
**Top-level** container per customer.

### Contents
- Entitlements (contracts, licenses)
- Users (global admins)
- Directories
- Subaccounts (directly, si no hay directories)
- Cost data
- Audit

### Best practice
- 1 Global Account per company
- Multi-national orgs may split by region if compliance requires

## Directory (opcional)
**Middle layer** for grouping.

### Use cases
- Department (Finance, HR, Sales)
- Environment tier (Dev, Test, Prod)
- Business unit
- Geographic region

### Setup
Global Account → **Create Directory**:
- Name
- Description
- Enable features (custom domain, entitlement management)

### Nested directories
Directories can contain sub-directories. Max ~5 levels.

### Permissions
Directory admins manage their subaccounts:
- Delegates authority
- Segregation of duties

## Subaccount
**Actual workspace** where you deploy apps.

### Attributes
- **Region**: fixed at create (can't change)
- **Environment**: CF, Kyma, ABAP (each is separate)
- **Users**: assigned via role collections
- **Entitlements**: which services
- **Subscriptions**

### Naming convention
- Include env: `myapp-dev`, `myapp-prod`
- Include region: `myapp-us-east-prod`
- Include team: `finance-integration-prod`

## Typical hierarchy example
```
Global Account: ACME Corp
├── Directory: Development
│   ├── Subaccount: finance-dev (Frankfurt)
│   ├── Subaccount: sales-dev (Frankfurt)
│   └── Subaccount: hr-dev (Netherlands)
├── Directory: Production
│   ├── Subaccount: finance-prod (Frankfurt)
│   ├── Subaccount: sales-prod (Frankfurt)
│   └── Subaccount: hr-prod (Netherlands)
└── Directory: Shared Services
    ├── Subaccount: sso-prod
    └── Subaccount: audit-log-prod
```

## Entitlements flow
- Assigned al Global Account (contract)
- Distributed to Directories (optional)
- Assigned al Subaccounts (final destination)

Quotas dividable:
- Contract: 100 GB HANA Cloud
- Directory Prod: 60 GB
- Directory Dev: 40 GB
- Each subaccount within directory subdivides

## Multi-region strategy
Use case: global company

### Option 1: Region per Directory
- Dir 'AMER' → subaccounts in US region
- Dir 'EMEA' → subaccounts in EU
- Dir 'APJ' → subaccounts in Asia

### Option 2: Region per Subaccount
- Fewer directories
- Subaccounts individually placed

Depends on org preference.

## Data isolation
- Each subaccount = separate boundary
- Data + user pool isolated
- Cross-subaccount comm requires explicit config (service consumption, destinations)

## Common patterns

### 3-tier landscape
- Dev → Test/QA → Prod

Each = separate subaccount. Deployment promotes app between.

### Hub-and-spoke
- Shared services (SSO, audit) in central 'hub' subaccount
- Business apps in 'spoke' subaccounts
- Spokes consume hub services

## Migration between subaccounts
Moving app from dev → prod:
- Redeploy code
- Reconfigure services
- Update DNS routes
- Users migration (manual re-invite)

No native 'move' feature. Design for multi-env from start.

## Common issues

### 'Entitlement not available in this subaccount'
- Not assigned at global/directory level
- Global admin needs to allocate

### 'Region not available'
- Some services region-limited (check availability matrix)
- May need to use different region

### 'Directory feature not enabled'
- Directory has optional features (entitlement mgmt, custom domain)
- Enable via directory settings

## Best practices
- Use directories for org clarity, not overuse (max 3-4 directory levels)
- Segregate prod/non-prod strictly (separate subaccounts, separate CF orgs)
- Central audit subaccount for compliance
- Naming: consistent, includes purpose + env

## Autorización
- Global Account admin: create/delete directories, subaccounts
- Directory admin: manage subaccounts within directory
- Subaccount admin: manage services + users within subaccount

RBAC nativo del cockpit.

title: SAP BTP: Cloud Foundry environment setup
tags: btp, cloud foundry, cf, org, space, cli
excerpt: Configurar CF environment y desplegar tu primer app.
body:
## Enable Cloud Foundry
Subaccount → **Cloud Foundry** → **Enable Cloud Foundry**.

Creates:
- CF Org (usually same name as subaccount)
- Assigns quota (CPU, RAM, routes)

## Create space
Space = namespace within Org.

Subaccount → **Spaces** → **New Space**:
- Name: `dev`, `qa`, `prod`
- Assign quota (subset of org quota)
- Assign users/roles

## Space roles
- **Space Developer** — deploy, manage apps
- **Space Manager** — permission mgmt
- **Space Auditor** — read-only

## Install CF CLI
### macOS
```bash
brew install cloudfoundry/tap/cf-cli@8
```

### Linux
```bash
curl -L 'https://packages.cloudfoundry.org/stable?release=linux64-binary&version=v8&source=github' | tar -zx
sudo mv cf8 /usr/local/bin/cf
```

### Windows
Download MSI from https://github.com/cloudfoundry/cli/releases

## Login
```bash
cf api https://api.cf.eu10.hana.ondemand.com
cf login
```

Provide user + password (or SSO).

### Target org + space
```bash
cf target -o my-org -s dev
```

## Deploy sample app

### 1. Create Node.js sample
```bash
mkdir hello-btp && cd hello-btp
```

**package.json**:
```json
{
    "name": "hello-btp",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "main": "app.js",
    "engines": { "node": "20.x" },
    "scripts": { "start": "node app.js" },
    "dependencies": { "express": "^4.18.0" }
}
```

**app.js**:
```javascript
const express = require('express');
const app = express();
app.get('/', (req, res) => res.send('Hello BTP!'));
const port = process.env.PORT || 3000;
app.listen(port, () => console.log(`Listening on ${port}`));
```

### 2. Manifest (opcional but recomendado)
**manifest.yml**:
```yaml
applications:
  - name: hello-btp
    memory: 128M
    instances: 1
    buildpacks:
      - nodejs_buildpack
    env:
      NODE_ENV: production
```

### 3. Push
```bash
cf push
```

CF:
- Uploads source
- Detects buildpack (Node.js)
- Installs deps (`npm install`)
- Starts app
- Assigns route (URL)

Output:
```
app hello-btp - deployed
route: https://hello-btp.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com
```

### 4. Test
```bash
curl https://hello-btp.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com
# Hello BTP!
```

## Buildpacks disponibles
- **nodejs_buildpack** — Node.js
- **java_buildpack** — Java (Spring, etc.)
- **python_buildpack** — Python
- **php_buildpack** — PHP
- **staticfile_buildpack** — static HTML/CSS/JS
- **binary_buildpack** — precompiled binary

## Ver apps
```bash
cf apps
```

## Ver logs
```bash
cf logs hello-btp --recent
cf logs hello-btp                # tail live
```

## Scale
```bash
cf scale hello-btp -i 3         # 3 instances
cf scale hello-btp -m 256M       # memory
cf scale hello-btp -k 1G         # disk
```

## Restart / restage
- **restart**: stop + start (env vars refresh)
- **restage**: rebuild with buildpack

```bash
cf restart hello-btp
cf restage hello-btp    # more thorough
```

## Env vars
```bash
cf set-env hello-btp APP_MODE production
cf restart hello-btp    # apply

cf env hello-btp        # ver todas
```

## Delete
```bash
cf delete hello-btp -f
```

## SSH al container
```bash
cf ssh hello-btp

# Once inside:
ls /home/vcap/app       # your code
ps aux                  # running processes
cat /etc/os-release     # OS info
```

## Common issues

### 'App won't start'
- Log muestra error
- Port binding: must listen on `PORT` env var
- Memory too low: increase
- Dependencies missing: check package.json

### 'Build failed'
- Buildpack can't detect language
- Add explicit `-b` flag: `cf push -b nodejs_buildpack`

### 'Route already in use'
- Rename route or delete existing

## Autorización
- Org Manager: create spaces, manage roles
- Space Developer: push apps
- Space Auditor: read-only

Manage via BTP cockpit → subaccount → **Spaces** → **Members**.

title: SAP BTP: services y service instances
excerpt: Consumir services (DB, Redis, auth) desde apps CF.
body:
## Marketplace
CF services catalog. Ver:

```bash
cf marketplace
```

Or BTP cockpit → subaccount → **Service Marketplace**.

### Services típicos
- **hana** — HANA Cloud (managed DB)
- **postgresql-db** — PostgreSQL
- **redis-cache** — Redis
- **connectivity** — SCC integration
- **destination** — destinations service
- **xsuaa** — XSUAA (auth)
- **application-logs** — centralized logging
- **audit-log-api** — audit trail
- **feature-flags** — feature flag management

## Create service instance
```bash
cf create-service hana schema my-db-instance
```

Params:
- Service name: `hana`
- Plan: `schema` (or `hdi-shared`, `admin`)
- Instance name: `my-db-instance`

CFcreates managed instance con name.

## Ver instances
```bash
cf services
cf service my-db-instance     # detail
```

## Bind service a app
Make service consumable from app:
```bash
cf bind-service my-app my-db-instance
cf restage my-app             # apply binding
```

Injects credentials en env var `VCAP_SERVICES` del app.

## Ver credentials injectados
```bash
cf env my-app

# Output includes VCAP_SERVICES:
{
    'hana': [{
        'name': 'my-db-instance',
        'credentials': {
            'host': 'xxx.hanacloud.ondemand.com',
            'port': 443,
            'user': 'DBADMIN',
            'password': '****',
            'schema': 'MYSCHEMA'
        }
    }]
}
```

App reads env var:
```javascript
const vcap = JSON.parse(process.env.VCAP_SERVICES);
const dbCreds = vcap.hana[0].credentials;
// use dbCreds.host, dbCreds.password, etc.
```

## Unbind
```bash
cf unbind-service my-app my-db-instance
cf restage my-app
```

## Delete service instance
```bash
cf delete-service my-db-instance -f
```

### With bindings
Must unbind first (or use `-f`).

## Service keys (para consumo externo)
Accessing service from outside CF (e.g., local dev):

```bash
cf create-service-key my-db-instance my-key
cf service-key my-db-instance my-key

# Prints credentials JSON
```

Use in local `.env` file para dev.

## Plans
Cada service tiene plans:
- Free tier (limited)
- Standard
- Enterprise (más features/quota)

### Cost
- Free plans: quota limits
- Paid: charged based on plan + usage

## Common services deep dive

### XSUAA (User Auth)
- OAuth 2.0 authorization server
- Handles user auth for apps
- Integrated with BTP identity

**Create**:
```bash
cf create-service xsuaa application my-xsuaa
```

Binds to app for auth flow.

### Destination service
Manages destinations (URLs, creds).

```bash
cf create-service destination lite my-destinations
```

Destinations config'd in cockpit, apps consume via this service.

### Connectivity service
Enables SCC tunnel access from CF apps.

```bash
cf create-service connectivity lite my-connectivity
```

Binding this service lets your app call onprem systems via SCC.

### Application Logs
Centralized log aggregation.

```bash
cf create-service application-logs lite my-logs
```

Logs go to Kibana dashboard.

## Manifest with services
Declare in `manifest.yml`:

```yaml
applications:
  - name: my-app
    services:
      - my-db-instance
      - my-xsuaa
      - my-destinations
      - my-connectivity
```

`cf push` auto-binds services listed.

## Update service instance
Migrate to different plan:
```bash
cf update-service my-db-instance -p enterprise
```

## Ver quota
Subaccount → **Entitlements** → ver max # instances per service.

CF quota per space limits total memory/routes.

## Common issues

### 'Service instance creation failed'
- Quota exceeded
- Region doesn't support that service
- Plan not enabled en entitlements

### 'Binding failed'
- App not in same space as instance
- Or app doesn't have permission to bind

### 'Credentials not injected'
- Restage required after bind
- Check `cf env` for VCAP_SERVICES presence

## Cross-space service sharing
By default, service instances tied to one space.

### Enable sharing
```bash
cf enable-feature-flag service_instance_sharing
cf share-service my-db-instance -s other-space -o other-org
```

Allows binding from apps en other spaces.

## Backup services
Service data:
- HANA: managed backups by SAP
- PostgreSQL: automatic backups en managed instances
- Redis: point-in-time recovery para some plans

Check service documentation for retention specifics.

title: SAP BTP: XSUAA — auth y user management
excerpt: Configurar OAuth 2.0 + roles con XSUAA service.
body:
## XSUAA
Extended Services (XS) User Authentication & Authorization.

Cloud-native fork of UAA (User Authentication and Authorization, Cloud Foundry standard).

Provides:
- OAuth 2.0 authorization server
- JWT token issuance
- User management (via IAS integration or Kerberos)
- Role/scope model

## Service instance
```bash
cf create-service xsuaa application my-xsuaa -c xs-security.json
```

### xs-security.json
```json
{
    'xsappname': 'my-app',
    'tenant-mode': 'dedicated',
    'scopes': [
        { 'name': '$XSAPPNAME.view', 'description': 'View data' },
        { 'name': '$XSAPPNAME.edit', 'description': 'Edit data' },
        { 'name': '$XSAPPNAME.admin', 'description': 'Admin' }
    ],
    'attributes': [
        { 'name': 'company', 'valueType': 'string' }
    ],
    'role-templates': [
        {
            'name': 'Viewer',
            'description': 'Read-only',
            'scope-references': ['$XSAPPNAME.view'],
            'attribute-references': ['company']
        },
        {
            'name': 'Editor',
            'description': 'Read + write',
            'scope-references': ['$XSAPPNAME.view', '$XSAPPNAME.edit']
        }
    ],
    'role-collections': [
        {
            'name': 'MyApp Admin',
            'description': 'Full access',
            'role-template-references': ['$XSAPPNAME.Editor']
        }
    ]
}
```

## Concepts

### Scope
Granular permission (e.g., `myapp.view`).

### Role template
Group of scopes.

### Role
Instance of role template (per subaccount).

### Role collection
Group of roles assigned to users.

### Attribute
Dynamic value passed via JWT (e.g., company ID for multi-tenancy).

## Bind app
```bash
cf bind-service my-app my-xsuaa
cf restage my-app
```

Credentials injected en `VCAP_SERVICES.xsuaa`.

## Auth flow (browser app)
1. User accesses app
2. App redirects to XSUAA login URL
3. XSUAA authenticates user (via IAS/AD)
4. XSUAA redirects back con auth code
5. App exchanges code for JWT access token
6. App uses token for subsequent API calls

## JWT structure
Header.Payload.Signature

Payload contains:
```json
{
    'user_name': 'jperez@empresa.com',
    'scope': ['myapp.view', 'myapp.edit'],
    'xs.user.attributes': {
        'company': ['1000']
    },
    'exp': 1234567890
}
```

## Validate JWT en app
```javascript
const xssec = require('@sap/xssec');
const xsenv = require('@sap/xsenv');

const uaaCreds = xsenv.getServices({ xsuaa: 'my-xsuaa' }).xsuaa;

app.use((req, res, next) => {
    xssec.createSecurityContext(req.headers.authorization, uaaCreds, (err, ctx) => {
        if (err) return res.status(401).send('Unauthorized');
        req.user = ctx;
        next();
    });
});

// Check scope
app.get('/data', (req, res) => {
    if (!req.user.checkScope('myapp.view')) return res.status(403).send('Forbidden');
    res.json({ data: 'sensitive' });
});
```

## Assign role collection a user
BTP cockpit → subaccount → **Security → Users** → seleccionar user → **Role Collections** → **Assign Role Collection**.

User must exist en subaccount (invited).

## Attribute-based access
Multi-tenant scenarios:
- User has attribute `company: 1000`
- App logic: solo show data for company 1000

Extract from JWT:
```javascript
const companyIds = req.user.getAttribute('company');
// Filter data
```

## IAS integration
XSUAA can delegate authentication to **SAP Identity Authentication Service (IAS)**:
- IAS handles user store + SSO
- XSUAA handles authorization (scopes, roles)

Configure IAS as trust in XSUAA:
- Subaccount → **Security → Trust Configuration** → **New Trust Configuration**

## Corporate IdP (SAML)
Integrate corporate SAML IdP (ADFS, Azure AD, Okta):
- SAML metadata trust
- Users authenticate via corp SSO
- SAP identifies user by email/other attribute

## Common issues

### 'Invalid token' during app call
- Token expired (check `exp`)
- Token signature invalid (XSUAA key rotation issue)
- Wrong app credentials (mismatch xsappname)

### 'User has no roles'
- Role collection not assigned
- Assignment done at wrong subaccount
- User email mismatch

### 'Redirect loop'
- Auth flow misconfigured
- Callback URL wrong
- Cookie issue (secure flag)

## Debug
```javascript
// Log token contents (dev only, never prod)
console.log(req.user.getTokenInfo().getPayload());
```

See scopes, attributes, exp.

## Best practices
- Never log JWT tokens en prod
- Use short-lived tokens (default 1 hour reasonable)
- Use refresh tokens for long sessions
- HTTPS only (never send tokens over HTTP)
- Scope minimally (least privilege)

## Advanced: OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials
For service-to-service (non-user):
```bash
curl -X POST https://<subaccount>.authentication.sap.hana.ondemand.com/oauth/token \
    -d 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
    -u '<client-id>:<client-secret>'

# Returns access_token for M2M calls
```

Used by cron jobs, integration apps calling other APIs.

## Federation
Multiple IdPs, federated trust:
- Corporate IdP (employees)
- Customer IdP (partners)
- Guest access

Configure multiple trust configs en subaccount.

title: SAP BTP: HANA Cloud
excerpt: Managed HANA en BTP: creación y uso.
body:
## SAP HANA Cloud
Managed HANA database service en BTP:
- In-memory column store
- Managed backups
- Auto-patching
- Scalable (vertical + horizontal)

## Provision
BTP cockpit → subaccount → **Instances and Subscriptions → SAP HANA Cloud**.

### Wizard
- Version: latest LTS o current
- Compute: 1x, 2x, 4x tier (memory + CPU)
- Storage: 240 GB min
- Availability zone
- Auto-start / auto-stop schedule
- Whitelisted IPs (optional)

### Cost
Per hour rate based on tier. Free tier no HANA Cloud (workaround: HANA Cloud trial).

## Access
Endpoint: `<instance-id>.hana.<region>.hanacloud.ondemand.com:443`

Port 443 SQL access. TLS mandatory.

## Client tools

### HANA Cloud UI (BTP cockpit)
SQL console web-based:
- Execute SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE
- Manage schemas, tables, views
- Ver stats en tiempo real

### SAP HANA Cockpit
Rich management UI, separate subscription.

### SAP HANA Studio (Eclipse)
Desktop client. Older but still functional.

### DBeaver / DataGrip
3rd-party SQL clients con HANA JDBC driver.

### Command line: hdbsql
```bash
hdbsql -n <endpoint>:443 -e -u DBADMIN -p <password>

# Once connected
> SELECT * FROM SYS.M_DATABASES;
```

## Schemas
### Default
- **SYSTEMDB** — system schema (no toques)
- **SYS** — system objects

### Custom
```sql
CREATE SCHEMA MYSCHEMA;
CREATE TABLE MYSCHEMA.USERS (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name NVARCHAR(100),
    email NVARCHAR(255)
);
```

## HDI containers
**HDI (HANA Deployment Infrastructure)** — recommended way to deploy schema con app.

### Create HDI container instance
```bash
cf create-service hana hdi-shared my-hdi
```

### Deploy schema via app
Define schema in `.hdbtable`, `.hdbview` files. Push app → HDI deploys.

Más sophisticated pattern for large apps.

## Connect from CF app
Bind service:
```bash
cf bind-service my-app my-hdi
```

App reads `VCAP_SERVICES`:
```javascript
const vcap = JSON.parse(process.env.VCAP_SERVICES);
const hana = vcap.hana[0].credentials;

const client = require('@sap/hana-client');
const conn = client.createConnection();
conn.connect({
    serverNode: `${hana.host}:${hana.port}`,
    uid: hana.user,
    pwd: hana.password,
    encrypt: true,
    sslValidateCertificate: false
});
```

## Backup & recovery
Managed automatically:
- Full daily
- Log backup every X min
- Retention: 7 days default, configurable up to 35

### Restore
BTP cockpit → HANA Cloud instance → **Actions → Restore**:
- Point-in-time (within retention window)
- Restores to new instance (keeps original)

## Users y roles
### System user
- **DBADMIN** — creado en provision
- Password: obtenido via BTP cockpit

### Create business users
```sql
CREATE USER JPEREZ PASSWORD 'ComplexPass123!' NO FORCE_FIRST_PASSWORD_CHANGE;
GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA MYSCHEMA TO JPEREZ;
```

### Roles
```sql
CREATE ROLE MYSCHEMA_READONLY;
GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA MYSCHEMA TO MYSCHEMA_READONLY;

GRANT MYSCHEMA_READONLY TO JPEREZ;
```

## SQL basics
### DML
```sql
SELECT * FROM users WHERE company = 1000;
INSERT INTO users (id, name) VALUES (1, 'Juan');
UPDATE users SET name = 'Juan Perez' WHERE id = 1;
DELETE FROM users WHERE id = 1;
```

### Aggregations
```sql
SELECT company, COUNT(*) AS count, AVG(salary) AS avg_salary
FROM employees
GROUP BY company
HAVING COUNT(*) > 10
ORDER BY avg_salary DESC;
```

### Analytical functions
```sql
SELECT id, name, salary,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rank
FROM employees;
```

## Column store vs row store

### Column store (default)
- Optimized for OLAP (analytical)
- Compression high
- Fast aggregations

### Row store
- Optimized for OLTP (transactional)
- Fast single-row lookups
- Use for high-frequency read/write of individual records

```sql
CREATE ROW TABLE ROW_TABLE_EXAMPLE (...);
CREATE COLUMN TABLE COL_TABLE_EXAMPLE (...);
```

## Scaling
### Vertical
BTP cockpit → HANA Cloud → **Modify** → increase tier.

### Horizontal (partitioning)
Large tables (>2 billion rows) require partitioning:
```sql
CREATE COLUMN TABLE huge_events (
    id BIGINT,
    date DATE,
    payload NVARCHAR(1000)
) PARTITION BY RANGE(YEAR(date)) (
    PARTITION VALUE = 2024,
    PARTITION VALUE = 2025,
    PARTITION VALUE = 2026
);
```

## Cost management
- **Auto-stop** during off-hours (dev environments)
- **Scale down** during weekends

Schedule en BTP cockpit → HANA Cloud → **Schedule**.

## Common issues

### 'Cannot connect'
- IP allowlist (add corporate IP)
- Instance stopped (start it)
- Firewall blocking 443 outbound

### 'Out of memory'
- Instance size too small
- Complex query using too much temp memory
- Scale up or optimize query

### 'Long-running query'
- Missing index
- Full table scan on huge table
- Check M_EXPENSIVE_STATEMENTS for culprits
